quests.definition: 'Eat into (something)' means to gradually but significantly reduce an amount of money or resources, often through repeated, ongoing expenses rather than one single cost.
quests.exampleSentence: The unexpected repair bills really ate INTO our savings this year.
quests.example: The unexpected repair bills really ate INTO our savings this year.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'INTO' combines with the verb 'EAT' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, borrowing the image of something being slowly consumed bite by bite until much less remains.
quests.nativeTip: This means gradually and significantly reducing a supply of money over time.

quests.definition: 'Dip into (something)' means to use a small amount of a reserve, such as savings, for a specific one-time need, unlike 'eat into,' which suggests a larger, ongoing erosion.
quests.exampleSentence: We had to dip INTO our emergency fund just to cover the deposit.
quests.example: We had to dip INTO our emergency fund just to cover the deposit.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'INTO' combines with the verb 'DIP' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, borrowing the image of dipping a hand briefly into a container rather than pouring the whole thing out.
quests.nativeTip: This means using a small portion of your savings for one specific purpose.

quests.definition: 'Eating into' fits the repeated, ongoing nature of monthly expenses steadily reducing savings, distinct from 'dipping into,' which suits a single, smaller withdrawal for a specific need.
quests.exampleSentence: A single emergency withdrawal was one thing, but month after month of expenses was seriously EATING INTO their savings.
quests.example: A single emergency withdrawal was one thing, but month after month of expenses was seriously EATING INTO their savings.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'EATING INTO' combines with the verb 'EAT' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase compares ongoing financial erosion to something being steadily consumed over time.
quests.nativeTip: This means a steady, ongoing reduction of savings, rather than one small, one-time withdrawal.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ EAT + EATING INTO ➔ EAT EATING INTO

quests.definition: 'Live off (something)' means to survive using a specific source of income or support over a long period, such as the proceeds from selling a business.
quests.exampleSentence: After selling the company, he lived OFF the profits for the rest of his life.
quests.example: After selling the company, he lived OFF the profits for the rest of his life.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'OFF' combines with the verb 'LIVE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, extended from the literal idea of living using a resource, here applied to ongoing financial support.
quests.nativeTip: This means surviving using a particular source of income over an extended period.

quests.definition: 'Live on (something)' fits a specific, often minimal diet consumed regularly, such as basic food during a trip, rather than a broader financial resource.
quests.exampleSentence: During the trip, we basically lived ON instant noodles and granola bars.
quests.example: During the trip, we basically lived ON instant noodles and granola bars.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'ON' combines with the verb 'LIVE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Literal in the sense that this food genuinely made up most of what was eaten during the trip.
quests.nativeTip: This means surviving mainly on a specific, often limited, type of food.

quests.definition: This reinforces 'live on' describing a student's typical simple, repetitive diet, distinct from the broader, longer-term financial dependency described by 'live off.'
quests.exampleSentence: As a student, she practically lived ON ramen and coffee.
quests.example: As a student, she practically lived ON ramen and coffee.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'ON' combines with the verb 'LIVE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Literal, as before — this genuinely was the primary food making up most meals during this period.
quests.nativeTip: This means surviving mainly on a simple, repetitive diet, similar to the sense taught earlier in this level.

quests.definition: 'Scrape by' means to barely manage to survive, often financially, implying more visible hardship than the milder 'get by.'
quests.exampleSentence: During the recession, many families could barely scrape BY .
quests.example: During the recession, many families could barely scrape BY .
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'BY' combines with the verb 'SCRAPE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, borrowing the image of scraping together the last remaining bits of something to just barely get enough.
quests.nativeTip: This means barely managing to survive financially, with real difficulty and hardship.

quests.definition: 'Make do (with something)' means to manage using an available but imperfect substitute, because the ideal option isn't accessible, such as using a tarp instead of a proper tent.
quests.exampleSentence: We didn't have a proper tent, so we had to make DO with a tarp and some rope.
quests.example: We didn't have a proper tent, so we had to make DO with a tarp and some rope.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'DO' combines with the verb 'MAKE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing is literally 'made' — the phrase describes accepting an imperfect substitute out of necessity.
quests.nativeTip: This means managing with an available but inadequate substitute, out of necessity.

quests.definition: 'Make do' fits using inferior available materials as a substitute, matching 'whatever leftover materials they could find.' 'Scrape by' and 'get by' both suit managing with limited money, not choosing physical substitute materials.
quests.exampleSentence: Rather than simply managing with what little they had, the family was forced to MAKE DO with whatever leftover materials they could find after the storm.
quests.example: Rather than simply managing with what little they had, the family was forced to MAKE DO with whatever leftover materials they could find after the storm.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'MAKE DO' combines with the verb 'MAKE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes accepting an imperfect substitute out of necessity.
quests.nativeTip: This means using whatever imperfect materials are available, out of necessity after a disaster.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ MAKE + MAKE DO ➔ MAKE MAKE DO

quests.definition: 'Fritter away (something)' means to waste money or time carelessly, bit by bit, usually on small, forgettable things rather than one big mistake.
quests.exampleSentence: He frittered AWAY his entire inheritance on lottery tickets and fast cars.
quests.example: He frittered AWAY his entire inheritance on lottery tickets and fast cars.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'AWAY' combines with the verb 'FRITTER' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing physically breaks into pieces — the phrase compares careless waste to something gradually disappearing in small amounts.
quests.nativeTip: This means wasting money carelessly, little by little, on things that don't matter much.

quests.definition: 'Frittered away' fits wasting money aimlessly on many small purchases, explicitly contrasted here with 'one meaningful splurge.' 'Splashed out' would actually describe that one deliberate, generous purchase instead.
quests.exampleSentence: Rather than treating herself to one meaningful splurge, she frittered FRITTERED AWAY her bonus on small, forgettable purchases throughout the year.
quests.example: Rather than treating herself to one meaningful splurge, she frittered FRITTERED AWAY her bonus on small, forgettable purchases throughout the year.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'FRITTERED AWAY' combines with the verb 'FRITTER' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase compares aimless, careless spending to something disappearing in many small pieces.
quests.nativeTip: This means wasting money on many small, forgettable things rather than one deliberate purchase.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ FRITTER + FRITTERED AWAY ➔ FRITTER FRITTERED AWAY

quests.definition: This extends 'fritter away' to time rather than money, showing the phrase applies to any valuable resource being carelessly wasted in small amounts.
quests.exampleSentence: It's easy to fritter AWAY a whole afternoon scrolling through your phone without noticing.
quests.example: It's easy to fritter AWAY a whole afternoon scrolling through your phone without noticing.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'AWAY' combines with the verb 'FRITTER' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase compares time slipping away unnoticed to a resource disappearing gradually.
quests.nativeTip: This means wasting time carelessly on something unproductive, without noticing how much has passed.

quests.definition: 'Stretch to (something)' means for a budget or amount of money to be just enough, or not quite enough, to cover a particular cost.
quests.exampleSentence: Our budget just won't stretch TO a beach vacation this year.
quests.example: Our budget just won't stretch TO a beach vacation this year.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'TO' combines with the verb 'STRETCH' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, borrowing the image of a limited amount of material being pulled and stretched to try to cover a larger area.
quests.nativeTip: This means a budget being just barely enough, or not enough, to cover a cost.

quests.definition: This reinforces 'stretch to,' showing that even a discount doesn't always make a budget large enough to reach a particular cost.
quests.exampleSentence: Even with the discount, our budget couldn't stretch TO the premium package.
quests.example: Even with the discount, our budget couldn't stretch TO the premium package.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'TO' combines with the verb 'STRETCH' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase compares a limited budget to material being pulled to try to cover more ground.
quests.nativeTip: This means a budget still falling short of covering a cost, even with a discount applied.

quests.definition: This reinforces 'stretch to,' describing a hopeful possibility that reducing other spending might make the remaining budget just enough for new furniture.
quests.exampleSentence: If we cut back elsewhere, our budget might just stretch TO new furniture for the living room.
quests.example: If we cut back elsewhere, our budget might just stretch TO new furniture for the living room.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'TO' combines with the verb 'STRETCH' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes a budget being pulled just far enough to cover an additional cost.
quests.nativeTip: This means a budget possibly being just enough to cover a cost, if other savings are made elsewhere.

quests.definition: 'Break even' means to reach a financial point where income exactly matches costs, so a business is neither losing nor gaining money.
quests.exampleSentence: After three tough years, the small business finally started to break EVEN .
quests.example: After three tough years, the small business finally started to break EVEN .
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'EVEN' combines with the verb 'BREAK' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing is literally broken — the phrase describes a financial balance point rather than any physical action.
quests.nativeTip: This means reaching a point where income exactly covers costs, with neither profit nor loss.

quests.definition: 'Cash in on (something)' means to profit from a situation or trend, often with a slightly critical tone suggesting the profit came a little too conveniently or opportunistically.
quests.exampleSentence: Several companies tried to cash IN ON the sudden popularity of home workouts.
quests.example: Several companies tried to cash IN ON the sudden popularity of home workouts.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'IN ON' combines with the verb 'CASH' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, borrowing the image of converting an opportunity directly into cash, as if trading it in.
quests.nativeTip: This means profiting from a situation or trend, sometimes in a way that feels a little opportunistic.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ CASH + IN ON ➔ CASH IN ON

quests.definition: This reinforces 'cash in on,' contrasted here with merely 'breaking even' from earlier in this level — actively profiting from a market surge is a step beyond just covering costs.
quests.exampleSentence: Instead of merely covering their costs, the smartest investors managed to cash IN ON the market's unexpected surge.
quests.example: Instead of merely covering their costs, the smartest investors managed to cash IN ON the market's unexpected surge.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'IN ON' combines with the verb 'CASH' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes turning a favorable situation directly into profit.
quests.nativeTip: This means going beyond simply covering costs to actively profit from favorable conditions.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ CASH + IN ON ➔ CASH IN ON

quests.definition: This reviews 'dip into' using the modal 'might have to,' describing a possible future need to use savings, rather than something that has already happened.
quests.exampleSentence: She might have to dip INTO her savings if the car repair costs as much as expected.
quests.example: She might have to dip INTO her savings if the car repair costs as much as expected.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'INTO' combines with the verb 'DIP' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes potentially using a small portion of savings for a specific need.
quests.nativeTip: This means possibly needing to use part of one's savings, expressed as a future possibility.

quests.definition: This reviews 'scrape by' using the modal 'could have,' describing an unrealized possibility — they had the option to struggle through on a smaller budget but chose to borrow instead.
quests.exampleSentence: They could have scraped BY on a smaller budget, but they chose to take out a loan instead.
quests.example: They could have scraped BY on a smaller budget, but they chose to take out a loan instead.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'BY' combines with the verb 'SCRAPE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes barely managing to survive financially, here as an unrealized option.
quests.nativeTip: This means they could have managed with real difficulty, but chose an easier path instead.

quests.definition: This reviews 'eat into' using the modal 'should never have,' expressing regret about a company allowing costs to seriously erode its profit margins.
quests.exampleSentence: The company should never have let its costs eat INTO profit margins so severely.
quests.example: The company should never have let its costs eat INTO profit margins so severely.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'INTO' combines with the verb 'EAT' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes profits being gradually and significantly reduced by rising costs.
quests.nativeTip: This means costs should never have been allowed to seriously reduce profits, expressed with regret about the past.

quests.definition: 'Scale back (something)' means to formally reduce the size or scope of a plan, project, or operation, often used in a fairly formal business context.
quests.exampleSentence: Due to the downturn, the company decided to scale BACK its expansion plans.
quests.example: Due to the downturn, the company decided to scale BACK its expansion plans.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'BACK' combines with the verb 'SCALE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing physical is measured — the phrase describes reducing the scale of an existing plan or operation.
quests.nativeTip: This means formally reducing the size or scope of a plan or operation.

quests.definition: 'Scale back' fits a formal, structural reduction affecting an entire department, distinct from 'cut back,' which more often describes smaller, individual expense reductions.
quests.exampleSentence: Rather than cutting individual expenses here and there, management chose to formally scale SCALE BACK the entire department's operations.
quests.example: Rather than cutting individual expenses here and there, management chose to formally scale SCALE BACK the entire department's operations.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'SCALE BACK' combines with the verb 'SCALE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes formally reducing the scope of an entire operation.
quests.nativeTip: This means formally reducing an entire department's scope, rather than cutting small individual costs.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ SCALE + SCALE BACK ➔ SCALE SCALE BACK

quests.definition: This reinforces 'scale back,' explicitly distinguished here from stopping something completely — the ventures continue, just at a reduced scale.
quests.exampleSentence: Investors were relieved when the firm decided to scale BACK its risky ventures instead of abandoning them completely.
quests.example: Investors were relieved when the firm decided to scale BACK its risky ventures instead of abandoning them completely.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'BACK' combines with the verb 'SCALE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes reducing scope while still maintaining some level of activity.
quests.nativeTip: This means reducing the scope of risky projects while still keeping them going in some form.

quests.definition: This reviews 'scale back' in the passive voice with a conditional modal — 'would have to be scaled back' — describing a hypothetical future reduction if funding fell through.
quests.exampleSentence: The project would have to be scaled BACK if funding fell through.
quests.example: The project would have to be scaled BACK if funding fell through.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'BACK' combines with the verb 'SCALE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes a possible future reduction in a project's scope.
quests.nativeTip: This means a project possibly being reduced in scope, expressed in the passive voice with a modal.

quests.definition: This reviews 'fritter away' in the past-perfect passive — 'had been frittered away' — describing wealth wasted gradually across two entire generations.
quests.exampleSentence: Much of the family fortune had been frittered AWAY over two generations of careless spending.
quests.example: Much of the family fortune had been frittered AWAY over two generations of careless spending.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'AWAY' combines with the verb 'FRITTER' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes wealth disappearing gradually through careless spending over time.
quests.nativeTip: This means a fortune having been wasted gradually over a long period, expressed in the past perfect passive.

quests.definition: This reviews 'break even' using the modal 'may never,' describing a worrying future possibility if rising costs aren't addressed.
quests.exampleSentence: If costs continue to rise, the business may never break EVEN .
quests.example: If costs continue to rise, the business may never break EVEN .
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'EVEN' combines with the verb 'BREAK' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes a financial balance point that might never be reached under current conditions.
quests.nativeTip: This means possibly never reaching the point where income covers costs, if current trends continue.

quests.definition: This revisits EAT INTO vs DIP INTO from earlier in this file. The phrase 'constant small subscriptions' describes an ongoing, repeated drain, matching 'eating into,' rather than a single small withdrawal, which would be 'dipping into.'
quests.exampleSentence: It wasn't one big expense that hurt them, but the constant small subscriptions slowly EATING INTO their monthly budget.
quests.example: It wasn't one big expense that hurt them, but the constant small subscriptions slowly EATING INTO their monthly budget.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'EATING INTO' combines with the verb 'EAT' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase compares small recurring costs to something being steadily consumed over time.
quests.nativeTip: This means small recurring costs steadily reducing a budget over time, not one small withdrawal or an active profit.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ EAT + EATING INTO ➔ EAT EATING INTO

quests.definition: This revisits SCALE BACK vs CUT BACK from earlier in this file. The formal, structural nature of the decision — affecting 'the entire research division' without shutting it down — points to 'scale back' rather than smaller-scale 'cutting back.'
quests.exampleSentence: Instead of trimming a few small costs, the board voted to formally scale BACK the entire research division without shutting it down completely.
quests.example: Instead of trimming a few small costs, the board voted to formally scale BACK the entire research division without shutting it down completely.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'BACK' combines with the verb 'SCALE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes formally reducing an entire operation's scope while keeping it running.
quests.nativeTip: This means a formal, structural reduction affecting an entire division, without eliminating it completely.

quests.definition: 'Make ends meet' means to earn just enough money to cover basic living expenses, without much left over. It's a fitting idiom to close this file, which has explored so many shades of financial struggle, resourcefulness, and careful management.
quests.exampleSentence: Even with two jobs, it was hard for the family to make ENDS MEET .
quests.example: Even with two jobs, it was hard for the family to make ENDS MEET .
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'ENDS MEET' combines with the verb 'MAKE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Fully figurative: no literal ends are joined — the phrase compares balancing income and expenses to two ends of something meeting exactly, with nothing left over.
quests.nativeTip: This means earning just barely enough money to cover basic living expenses.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ MAKE + ENDS MEET ➔ MAKE ENDS MEET
